title: Nico and the Paper Unicorn
markdown:
Nico the dormouse loved naps. He knew the best moss in the Whispering Woods, the warmest sunbeams, the coziest hollows where toast-colored fur could vanish into toast-colored dark. Most mornings he stretched, yawned a yawn that showed his pink tongue, and went straight back to sleep. That was a perfect day.

Then he found an old picnic basket, forgotten under ferns, and inside it a clean white piece of paper. He had never seen paper. He sniffed it. Sunshine, and something that did not smell like moss at all. His paws, used to berries and beetles, proved good at creases. Fold, fold, fold: a flowing mane, graceful legs, a pointy horn. A unicorn.

With a soft rustle the unicorn lifted its head. Two dark-dot eyes blinked. Hello, it said, in a voice like leaves after rain. I am Comet.

Nico’s nose wiggled. The paper had spoken. A paper unicorn, he squeaked, and Comet tossed a paper head so the mane rippled. Yes. And you are a dormouse. Listen close: we must race to the tallest hill before the sun comes up. Super important.

Nico’s heart jumped like a butterfly in a jar. Race. Tallest hill. Before morning. A long way for short legs. It was almost time for his second nap. The burrow waited, mossy and kind. Being awake and far from bed muddled him. Comet was already prancing, light as if the air had agreed to carry him. No time for naps. The hill is waiting. The sun is coming, and we must see it from the very top. A paper nose nudged Nico, gentle, and they were off.

The woods were quiet and dim, the kind of quiet Nico usually slept through. He scurried, short legs as fast as they would go, paws almost silent on the soft ground. Comet, light as a feather, glided beside him. They reached a brook, wide and bubbling, moonlight sparkling in the water. Nico gulped. Water was wet. Naps were dry. Comet trotted to the edge as if wetness were a rumor. Watch, he called, and leaned, and his paper body bent into a strong smooth bridge. Nico held his breath and tiptoed. Wobbly, like a thin leaf. The water whispered under him. One paw. Then another.

A patch of tall flowers nodded, petals drooping toward sleep. Comet tried to hurry through, paper hooves a soft rustle. Nico walked very slowly, nose full of sweet sleepy air. Careful, Comet, he whispered, and the flowers were allowed to keep their dreams.

Dark clouds gathered like a rumpled blanket. A low rumble shook the ground. Wind whistled the trees. Nico shivered. He hated wind. It mussed fur and made a burrow feel drafty. Maybe we should go back, he said, voice small. The sun will be there tomorrow. My burrow is warm. Safe from this blowy mess. He could almost smell dry leaves and comforting dark.

Comet stopped. Paper body catching faint moonlight, horn a thin bright line, dark-dot eyes sure. He did not argue. He only stood there, a little wind-blown, believing in the hill. Nico’s heart felt heavy. He could not let his friend down. Not now. Okay, Comet, he said, and the breath he took tasted like rain. We’ll keep going. For the tallest hill.

At the bottom the wind made standing hard. Long grass swayed like a stormy sea. Comet’s edges fluttered. Grit on Nico’s whiskers. A roar in his ears. The sky was bruised purple, with a sliver of pink at the world’s edge. So close, Comet cried, thin against the weather, still glad. The hill was steep, grass and loose stone. The wind pushed them back. Something quiet and strong rose in Nico that was not sleepiness and not worry. He looked at Comet, a paper light in the wild, and knew.

Come on, Comet. He dug tiny claws into earth, found grip, pushed. He nudged Comet’s paper side, up, up. The wind tried to lift the unicorn like a kite. Nico pressed against him, a small shield, and gave the climb his whole self. Grass scratched. The sky painted itself wild. His heart thumped with purpose instead of fear.

Then they were there. The top. The sun, orange and pink, touching the world, chasing night. The wind softened and carried dew and waking earth. Comet stood tall, mane catching new light, horn a proud thin shine. Nico, breathless and dusty, looked out. The woods below were a green carpet in gold, brand new.

We did it, Comet said, joy as bright as the sunrise. We reached the tallest hill.

Nico did not count the missed nap. He smiled, wide, at his paper friend, and felt a warmth brighter than any sunbeam he had ever slept in. He had not only followed. He had been the weight that kept the wind from winning. On that hilltop, as the world woke, Nico the dormouse was still a napper. He was also, now, an adventurer who knew the way home would still be there after the light.
